subject: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@vendr.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the quick intro call last week. We’re starting a short sprint to onboard EvoBank’s security evidence into Vendr and want to confirm the preferred delegation pattern and ingestion method before we hand off the bulk manifest.

Quick context: EvoBank will provide a signed manifest of artifacts (SOC 2, SIG fragments, CAIQ exports, KMS-signed fingerprints) and we want Vendr to accept either (A) an S3 pre-signed ingest with a service account, or (B) API upload using a short-lived service principal.

Can you confirm the following so we can finalize the handoff checklist?
- Which fields in your delegation CSV map to "evidence_owner" vs "uploader" vs "signer" (we'll attach our draft manifest).
- Do you accept a KMS-signed JSON manifest that lists S3 object hashes (SHA256) for proof-of-possession?
- What TTL do you enforce on temporary credentials and can you automate a 30-day expiry for the portal-uploader role?

I’ve attached our current manifest export (rfq_vendr_manifest.csv) — it’s intentionally broad; Marissa will annotate what needs immediate sign-off vs long-tail archival.

Action we’re asking from Vendr: reply with the delegation template you prefer + a short confirmation of signed-manifest acceptance. If everything looks good we’ll schedule a 60-minute handover session with EvoBank’s security team.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: rfq_vendr_manifest.csv (CSV stub, 42 rows)
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@vendr.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vendr Portal Support <support@vendr.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 10:03:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the clear checklist and the manifest. Short answers up front:
- We can handle both ingestion paths (S3 pre-signed + API). For bulk onboarding we recommend S3 pre-signed with a short-lived service account that has the "portal-uploader" role.
- We accept KMS-signed manifests that include SHA256 hashes; you can upload the manifest as metadata or as a top-level file.
- TTL: defaults are 14 days for pre-signed uploads; we can extend to 30 days for enterprise handoffs on a case-by-case basis (we’ll mark this in the provisioning ticket).

I’ve attached our delegation template (vendr-delegation-template.csv) — it shows the exact column names we use: principal_email, role, scope, owner_flag, signature_required. Please map your manifest to these columns.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rafael/Marissa map your manifest to our CSV and return it to us.
2) We provision a portal-uploader service account (30d TTL) and share credentials via our secure ticket.
3) We run a dry-run ingest with 5 representative artifacts to validate hashing and signed-manifest acceptance.

I’ll loop in our engineering contact on step 3 if we need tighter S3 ACLs.

Cheers,
Lena Ortiz
Partner Success, Vendr
Lena Ortiz | Vendr

Attachment: vendr-delegation-template.csv (template stub)
Related: https://vendr.com/docs/portal-delegation-guide
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@vendr.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2027 11:22:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA

Thanks — looping in a few clarifications from our side. I annotated the manifest with a priority column to help the dry-run focus:
- Priority = P0: SOC 2 Type II report + current SIG questionnaire fragments flagged by EvoBank security. These must be verified and signed in the portal.
- Priority = P1: CAIQ exports and system architecture diagrams for reference (ingest but mark as informational).
- Evidence ownership: we propose these fields on the delegation template: evidence_owner (business contact), technical_contact (for upload troubleshooting), and attestation_signer (who can mark evidence as verified).

Attachment: evidence-manifest-annotated.xlsx — I left comments next to the top 12 rows that should be included in the dry-run.

Two asks for Vendr:
1) Can the portal expose a CSV output we can import back into our trackers that contains vendr_artifact_id + manifest_hash + ingestion_timestamp? That will help our compliance team reconcile possession.
2) If the manifest is accepted, can you provide an audit event sample for the uploaded object (event fields we’ll use for our SIEM ingestion)?

Thanks — Marissa will run the mapping exercise and return a mapped CSV by EOD tomorrow.

—
Marissa Cole
Security Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@vendr.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2027 16:45:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA

Lena / team — quick technical clarifications from infra:

On Tue, Dec 21, 2027 at 11:22 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attachment: evidence-manifest-annotated.xlsx — I left comments next to the top 12 rows that should be included in the dry-run.

We’re fine with S3 pre-signed + KMS-signed manifest, but please confirm these two points so our automation can be configured correctly:
- Signed manifest format: we will emit a JSON with a top-level "manifest_version" and an array of objects: {"path": "s3://...", "sha256": "...", "size": 12345, "logical_id": "SOC2-2026"}. Will Vendr accept manifest_version 2 (minor versioning) and ignore unknown fields?
- Audit schema: we need a sample JSON audit event for ingestion to map fields to our SIEM. Suggested fields: artifact_id (vendr_artifact_id), logical_id, uploader_principal, manifest_hash, ingestion_ts, object_etag. If you can paste a sample event we’ll wire our forwarder.

If you confirm those two, we’ll hand off a pre-signed S3 bucket with a 30-day lifecycle and a manifest file keyed to /incoming/evidence-manifests/evobank-20271220.json.

—
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@vendr.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Vendr Portal Support <support@vendr.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendr portal: delegation matrix & evidence QA

Karthik / Marissa / Rafael —

Thanks for the details. Confirmations below and next steps:

- Manifest format: Vendr accepts manifest_version 2 and will ignore unknown fields. Your JSON example is fine — please include SHA256 and logical_id.
- Audit schema: example event we emit on successful ingest:
  {"event_type": "artifact_ingest", "vendr_artifact_id": "VA-48291", "logical_id": "SOC2-2026", "uploader_principal": "portal-uploader@vendr.com", "manifest_hash": "sha256:...", "ingestion_ts": "2027-12-22T15:00:12Z", "object_etag": "3f7a9b..."}

Operational notes: we will provision a portal-uploader service account with 30-day TTL and role scoping to the EvoBank portal only. We will not retain plaintext credentials in the ticket; credentials will be delivered via our secure vault.

Action items (agreed):
- Marissa: return the mapped CSV using our template (vendr-delegation-template.csv).
- Rafael: coordinate the EvoBank dry-run window (we recommend Jan 4–6).
- Vendr: provision service account and schedule dry-run once we receive the mapped CSV.

I attached a signed manifest stub for your records (delegation-signed-manifest.json) and a link to a shared folder with our onboarding runbook.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Partner Success, Vendr

Attachment: delegation-signed-manifest.json (signed-manifest stub)
